newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway central bank leaves CPI forecasts unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Norway central bank leaves CPI forecasts unchanged.

text.p: Norway's Central Bank said on Wednesday it forecast inflation at 1.25 percent in 1996 and 2.5 percent in 1997, unchanged from previous projections.

In its third quarter report, the bank said consumer price inflation may reach three percent this winter as a result of recent increases in electricity prices. But it would edge down in the following period, it said.
Excluding the rise in power prices, inflation was projected to rise to 2.5 percent towards the end of 1997.
"The increase in price inflation primarily reflects a higher level of wage growth," a statement from the bank said.
Estimates for rises in wage growth were unchanged from its June report at 4.25 percent this year to five per in 1997.
Mainland gross domestic product (GDP) forecasts for 1996 also were unchanged at 3.25 percent. Mainland GDP in 1997 was seen at 2.5 percent.

The bank said it projected a rise in capacity utilisation in 1996 and 1997. Robust growth in real income and a decline in the household saving ratio would contribute to growth in consumption, while growth in traditional merchandise exports appeared to be higher than expected, it said.
Central Bank Governor Kjell Storvik said that fiscal tightening and a resumption of wage moderation were necessary to avoid rising price and wage inflation.

"Growth in the Norwegian economy is now considerably stronger than among our European trading partners, which makes it more demanding than otherwise to maintain price and wage inflation on a par with our trading partners," Storvik said in a statement.

"The risk of further pressures in the economy next year underlines the need for a tight fiscal policy stance in 1997, which is at least in line with the tightening originally called for in the budget of 1996."
The government is due to present its proposed national budget for 1997 to parliament on October 4.
